problem: Evaluating complex, end-to-end website development from visual designs remains limited despite advances in coding agents.
approach: Introduces Vision2Web, a hierarchical benchmark spanning static UI-to-code, interactive multi-page frontend, and full-stack development, with dual verification via GUI agent and VLM-based judge.
contribution: A 193-task benchmark from real-world websites with 918 prototype images and 1,255 test cases, revealing substantial performance gaps in state-of-the-art models on full-stack tasks.

problem: Post-training backdoor detectors fail when non-target classes naturally exhibit extreme detection statistics or when backdoors are subtle.
approach: Proposes Class Subspace Orthogonalization (CSO), a constrained optimization method that suppresses intrinsic class features while preserving backdoor trigger signals.
contribution: A plug-and-play detector enhancement that improves sensitivity across multiple existing backdoor detectors by orthogonalizing away intrinsic features.

problem: Sparse attention assumes memory-bound decoding, but new architectures like MLA and MTP have made decoding compute-bound, introducing inefficiency.
approach: TileSparse applies arithmetic-intensity-aware sparsity with QK 2D sparsity and Tiered patterns optimized for compute tile size rather than fetched tokens.
contribution: Improves accuracy by 40% over dynamic K-only methods under tight budgets and preserves 99% full-attention accuracy while cutting compute by 40.8%.

problem: Reasoning models waste user time by generating lengthy hidden reasoning before any visible response when starting from false premises.
approach: PLANTAIN teaches models via post-training to externalize step-by-step plans before reasoning, enabling early feedback and intervention.
contribution: Improves pass@1 by roughly 6% on average across math, coding, text-to-SQL, and reading benchmarks while reducing time-to-first-response by over 60%.

problem: Categorical data generation requires discrete transitions, making few-step distillation difficult compared to continuous diffusion models.
approach: Categorical Flow Maps define continuous flow trajectories toward a simplex with endpoint consistency training and guidance-compatible inference.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art few-step results on images, molecular graphs, and text with strong single-step generation performance.

problem: Crystal modeling tasks like CSP and DNG lack unified frameworks that share representations across different generation objectives.
approach: Multimodal Crystal Flow (MCFlow) uses independent time variables for atom types and structures with composition- and symmetry-aware atom ordering.
contribution: A single model competitive with task-specific baselines on MP-20 and MPTS-52 across crystal structure prediction, de novo generation, and atom type prediction.

problem: Learning structured probability distributions like juntas and quantum junta states requires sample-efficient algorithms.
approach: Develops learning algorithms for k-junta distributions with total variation error bound, quantum junta states with trace distance error, and QAC0 circuits using optimal Pauli analysis.
contribution: Quadratic improvement on prior upper bounds for junta learning and improved QAC0 circuit learning; provides matching lower bounds for quantum juntas.

problem: LLM agents are constrained by context length on long-horizon tasks and rely on manually defined context management pipelines.
approach: Context Folding empowers agents to procedurally manage context by branching into sub-trajectories and folding them upon completion; FoldGRPO trains this via RL with process rewards.
contribution: Matches baseline performance on long-horizon tasks while using 10x smaller active context and outperforms models constrained to the same context size.

problem: Heterogeneous multivariate time series lack general-purpose representation learning approaches that handle diverse sensor modalities.
approach: CHARM (Channel-Aware Representation Model) incorporates channel-level textual descriptions into a JEPA-trained transformer with description-aware gating and temporal stability loss.
contribution: Strong performance across anomaly detection, classification, forecasting using only linear probes; text descriptions enable cross-dataset generalization.

problem: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) training exhibits instability due to geometric conflict between plasticity and stability gradients.
approach: Probabilistic Conflict Resolution (PCR) models gradients as random variables and uses uncertainty-aware soft projection to dynamically arbitrate conflicts.
contribution: Significantly smooths training trajectory and achieves superior performance on various reasoning tasks.

problem: Evaluating interactive frontend games lacks scalable mechanisms that verify dynamic interactivity without prohibitive computational costs.
approach: ALIVE uses one-shot planning and DOM-based analysis for automatic evaluation at scale, producing high-quality SFT data and RL reward signals.
contribution: Significantly outperforms static baselines while remaining orders of magnitude more efficient than GUI agents; enables ALIVE-Coder with superior interactive code generation.

problem: Aligning large language models remains challenging, typically requiring training-time interventions or expensive inference-time procedures.
approach: Alignment-Aware Decoding (AAD) enhances alignment at inference without specialized training beyond standard DPO, through implicit reward optimization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms strong baselines across alignment benchmarks and model scales; generates high-quality synthetic data for improving alignment in data-constrained settings.

problem: Knowledge graph inference assumes nearly all fact components are known, but real scenarios involve multiple missing components.
approach: KREPE uses masked discrete diffusion to model probability distributions of missing components via contextual message passing and context aggregation.
contribution: State-of-the-art on standard HKG link prediction and outperforms LLM baselines in generating novel correct facts from arbitrary masked queries.

problem: Conformal prediction methods with localization produce prediction sets with high variability in size, especially with limited calibration data.
approach: Stable Conformal Prediction (StCP) uses transfer learning from labeled source-task data and unlabeled target data to improve set stability without additional target labels.
contribution: Delivers more stable prediction sets than standard conformal methods, especially for localized approaches when calibration data are limited.

problem: Vision transformer finetuning benefits remain poorly understood, particularly regarding the role of architectural smoothness in transfer learning.
approach: Analyzes component plasticity (rate of change to input perturbations) as a metric distinct from smoothness, showing high plasticity in attention and feedforward layers aids finetuning.
contribution: Over 1,000 finetuning runs show attention and feedforward plasticity consistently leads to better performance, departing from the prevailing smoothness preference.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle with fine-grained perception in ultra-high-resolution images, particularly for tiny objects, lacking both prior guidance and posterior correction.
approach: BVS (Bayesian Visual Search) formulates perception as global optimization over spatial-scale manifold, using MLLM attention rollout for priors and GP-UCB with scale-aware kernels for posterior correction.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines with superior accuracy-efficiency trade-off and provides sub-linear regret bounds.

problem: Sliding-window streaming multi-armed bandits require balancing sample efficiency, regret, and memory constraints in single-pass settings.
approach: Analyzes pure exploration and regret minimization with memory-regret trade-offs, proving hard instances for sublinear memory and providing efficient approximation algorithms.
contribution: Sharp memory-regret trade-offs for single-pass algorithms and efficient approximate best-arm finding under limited memory.

problem: Backdoor attacks in LLMs are difficult to defend against because hidden triggers remain obscured even after safety training.
approach: Proposes an inversion-inspired reinforcement learning framework enabling poisoned LLMs to introspectively reverse-engineer their own triggers, followed by mitigation strategies.
contribution: Demonstrates strong potential to improve LLM robustness against backdoor risks across five backdoor attacks compared to six baseline methods.

problem: Robust optimization requires specifying robustness levels a priori, often chosen ad hoc, leading to insufficient protection or excessive conservativeness.
approach: Constructs data-driven uncertainty sets via conformal prediction with distribution-free guarantees on miscoverage-regret Pareto frontiers, guiding robustness calibration.
contribution: Provides finite-sample guarantees enabling practitioners to reliably evaluate and calibrate robustness according to cost-risk preferences.

problem: Byzantine failures and data poisoning in distributed learning show similar optimization guarantees, but their generalization impact remains unclear.
approach: Provides tight algorithmic stability analysis comparing generalization degradation under both threat models.
contribution: Proves Byzantine failures yield strictly worse generalization rates than data poisoning with additive degradation of Θ(f/(n-f)) vs Ω(sqrt(f/(n-2f))).

problem: Multimodal SSL methods assume redundancy across views, but heterogeneous real-world data (e.g., healthcare) lacks this and can amplify bias.
approach: FairSSL leverages data heterogeneity via subject-aware variance-invariance-covariance regularization with segment-based pooling and representation decorrelation.
contribution: Significantly improves fairness on heterogeneous multimodal datasets without sacrificing downstream predictive performance.

problem: Existing activation analysis methods like PCA and sparse autoencoders impose strong structural assumptions.
approach: Trains diffusion meta-models on one billion residual stream activations to learn the distribution of neural network internal states without structural constraints.
contribution: Meta-model's learned prior improves steering intervention fluency; neurons isolate concepts with sparse probing scores scaling with model loss.

problem: Safety constraints are often implicit and unmeasurable during training, leaving RL agents unable to learn fine-grained safety from coarse trajectory-level labels.
approach: TraCeS learns per-timestep violation credit from trajectory-level labels using a sequential violation estimator whose credits factorize trajectory safety probability.
contribution: Improves constraint satisfaction and feedback efficiency over baselines across continuous-control benchmarks, including long-horizon and noisy-label settings.

problem: Token-level reweighting for supervised finetuning uses one-dimensional indicators, missing both target-specific alignment and intrinsic uncertainty.
approach: RankTuner compares ground-truth token rank to expected rank under model distribution, using Relative Rank Indicator and Relative Scale for selective reweighting.
contribution: Consistent improvements on mathematical reasoning, transfer gains on OOD reasoning, and better code generation over probability- or entropy-only baselines.

problem: Set representation learning methods fail when deployed models encounter element-level degradations like outliers or missing components.
approach: SW-DRSO applies distributionally robust optimization with a barycentric adversary approximating worst-case corrupted sets via differentiable training-time simplex weighting.
contribution: Effectively enhances robustness against corruption across four tasks while maintaining high overall performance.

problem: Sampling from unnormalized multimodal distributions with limited density evaluations remains difficult despite existing approaches like Parallel Tempering.
approach: Conditional Diffusion Sampling combines Parallel Tempering and diffusion transport via Conditional Interpolants with exact, closed-form SDE and no neural training.
contribution: Achieves superior sample quality to density evaluation cost trade-offs compared to state-of-the-art samplers.

problem: Existing watermarking methods for model extraction defense require retraining and lack clear theoretical foundations against adaptive attacks.
approach: Neural Honeytrace is a plug-and-play watermarking framework using training-free multi-step transmission leveraging long-tailed backdoor learning.
contribution: Reduces queries for worst-case ownership verification to 2% of existing methods with zero training cost.

problem: Open-ended reward modeling for RL relies on costly proprietary systems or lacks interpretability; existing generative reward models are limited by static criteria.
approach: UniRRM uses staged reasoning chains to dynamically generate task-generic and instruction-specific criteria for multiple languages and evaluation paradigms.
contribution: Achieves near state-of-the-art performance across benchmarks on comparable model sizes and remains effective for unseen evaluation paradigms.

problem: Video generation poses escalating detection challenges; multimodal LLMs lack fine-grained perception despite strong reasoning.
approach: VideoVeritas integrates Joint Preference Alignment and Perception Pretext Reinforcement Learning using spatiotemporal grounding and object counting as perception pretext tasks.
contribution: Achieves balanced performance across diverse benchmarks with a new MintVid dataset of 3K videos from nine generators plus factual-error annotations.

problem: Multimodal LLMs face safety concerns from cross-modal interactions and struggle with implicit-risk detection due to data scarcity and reward hacking.
approach: Meerkat-VL introduces Normative Perceptual Self-Verification and Dual-Objective Perceptual Consistency Alignment with Meerkat-Safe dataset for implicit-risk training.
contribution: Improves safety and helpfulness by 16% and 13% on multimodal benchmarks and achieves 32% safety gain on implicit-risk tasks.

problem: Mental rotation, a fundamental human spatial reasoning ability, lacks mechanistic models grounded in behavioral data.
approach: Proposes a three-component mechanistic model combining equivariant neural encoder for 3D representations, neuro-symbolic object encoder, and decision agent with VR-informed design.
contribution: Captures human mental rotation performance, response times, and behavior across this work and others' experiments with demonstrated component necessity.

problem: LLM pre-training is approaching data limits (Data Wall), requiring dynamic selection of high-quality tokens rather than more tokens.
approach: OPUS (Optimizer-induced Projected Utility Selection) scores candidates in optimizer-induced update space with Ghost/CountSketch for efficiency and Boltzmann sampling for diversity.
contribution: Outperforms previous methods across diverse corpora, quality tiers, optimizers, and scales; incurs only 4.7% compute overhead.

problem: LLM reasoning patterns remain opaque and RL assigns uniform credit across generations, obscuring pivotal steps.
approach: Uses attention analysis to distinguish locally and globally focused heads, revealing a preplan-and-anchor pattern with dynamic credit assignment to critical nodes.
contribution: Three novel RL strategies show consistent performance gains across reasoning tasks by targeting preplan tokens, anchor tokens, and their temporal coupling.

problem: Improving reasoning in diffusion language models via reinforcement learning requires accurate trajectory likelihood estimates.
approach: d2 introduces policy gradient algorithms with trajectory likelihood estimators tailored to model classes: d2-AnyOrder for any-order decoding and d2-StepMerge for standard masked diffusion.
contribution: Sets state-of-the-art for DLMs on logical reasoning (Countdown, Sudoku) and math reasoning (GSM8K, MATH500) with significant improvements over RL baselines.

problem: Language models can deliberately underperform on capability evaluations (sandbagging), evading safety measures by exploiting evaluation inconsistencies.
approach: Cross-Context Consistency (C3) is an unsupervised black-box framework exploiting asymmetry: true incapability shows consistent confusion across paraphrased questions, while feigned incompetence creates detectable inconsistencies.
contribution: Maintains classification signal where existing methods fail across prompted and fine-tuned sandbagging scenarios.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models struggle in long-horizon and OOD scenarios due to lack of explicit multimodal reasoning and action anticipation mechanisms.
approach: HALO enables embodied multimodal chain-of-thought via Mixture-of-Transformers architecture decoupling semantic reasoning, visual foresight, and action into specialized experts.
contribution: Surpasses baseline on RoboTwin by 25.9%; shows strong generalization under aggressive environment randomization.

problem: Reconstructing continuous dynamics from sparse, non-contiguous, unpaired point cloud snapshots remains difficult due to propagation errors and temporal discontinuity.
approach: FlowCloud uses variational Neural ODE to aggregate all observed timepoints into joint latent representation, trained with Sinkhorn distance, Chamfer distance, trajectory regularization, and supervised losses.
contribution: Improves interpolation accuracy and promising short-term extrapolation performance on human motion and developmental biology datasets.

problem: Attention mechanism deployment is expensive due to quadratic resource requirements scaling with sequence length.
approach: WildCat compresses attention by attending over small weighted coreset selected via randomly pivoted Cholesky with optimal weighting for reconstruction error.
contribution: Achieves super-polynomial error decay O(n^(-sqrt(log(log(n))))) with near-linear O(n^(1+o(1))) runtime while preserving 99% full-attention accuracy and cutting compute by 40.8%.

problem: Analyzing last-iterate convergence for stochastic proximal algorithms typically requires stringent bounded variance assumptions.
approach: Analyzes proximal stochastic gradient and randomized incremental proximal methods under componentwise convexity and smoothness.
contribution: Proves Õ(1/√T) convergence rate for last iterate under relaxed bounded variance assumptions; applies to graph-guided regularizers in federated learning.

problem: K-means clustering lacks typical-case analysis capturing real-world instance characteristics.
approach: Adopts manifold hypothesis where data concentrates on low-dimensional manifolds and designs Qkmeans seeding exploiting quantization exponent scaling laws.
contribution: Provides O(ρ^(-2) log k) approximate solutions in time O(nD log k) + Õ(ρ^(-1)k^(1+γ)) with novel runtime-quality trade-offs validated across domains.
